objective: CDN peering lifecycle from service registration through peering initiation, negotiation, resource discovery, operational management, and disband/re-arrangement
decision_strategy: Model mutually exclusive branches with explicit guards.
Use a single integrated lifecycle from registration through termination.
Represent retries as a loop with renegotiation body and successful exit when sufficient resources are acquired.
concurrency_strategy: Use one fork for the established peering operational setup.
Perform configuration advertising, load exchange, request redirection, accounting exchange, and policy enforcement in parallel, then synchronize before refusal/termination checks.
exception_strategy: Policy rejection prevents passing service requirements to the Local Peering Agent.
Insufficient resources trigger reevaluation and renegotiation.
Operational refusal by a peer terminates the arrangement.
Exceptional circumstances bypass disband/re-arrangement and end the scenario.
termination_strategy: Normal completion ends after operational management when no refusal or termination condition applies.
Failure and exceptional paths terminate at explicit final nodes.
Disband or re-arrangement ends at a final node after the Local Peering Agent acts.
